checking.description:
Ticket 423 round 2: an `account_check` reply whose check is still queued for a probe slot (`signed_in` unknown):
the page shows Checking and asks again.

fell_back.description: Ticket 358: on "Your own" when the picked default's account is gone and new sessions fell back here.

plan.description: Ticket 323: the plan word from the status command of a signed-in Claude account (`max`); absent otherwise.

session_default.description: The owner picked this account for new sessions of its agent (`settings.json` `features` `accounts.default.<agent>`).

oneOf.description: Orca's "did not accept that code": the login exited non-zero after a pasted code.
The login exited 0, but the status command does not say signed in.
Signed-in state unreadable: a new folder is kept (registered), never deleted on a guess.
The new account's folder is kept, but the account list could not be saved.

AccountSigninState.description: What the page shows for one attempt.

account.description: The account, once signed in (or kept because its state could not be read).

link.description: The sign-in link, once it passed the allowlist (opened in the browser and offered by Copy link).

paste.description: The login reads a pasted code (Claude); Codex finishes through its own local callback only.

AcpModel.description: Ticket 358: one model an agent reported in its Session Config Options; `value` goes back to it exactly as it came.

AcpRow.description: One row of Settings > Agents' ACP table.

acp.description: False: a terminal-only CLI (no chat view or waiting detection).

diagnostics.description: What 진단 복사 copies (`diagnostics`). Never a variable's value.

display.description: Ticket 358: the owner's name for this entry, when one is set (`label` already shows it).

docs_url.description: The tool's https pages, from `known.toml` only: never from the agent or `agents.toml`.

efforts.description: Ticket 994: the thinking levels it last reported, lowest first as it listed them; empty: it has none.

env_set.description: Per name in `env`: whether the core has a value to pass. Never the value.

models.description: Ticket 358: the models this agent last reported; empty: it reported none, or never ran.

setup.description: A listed agent's add steps (none for a custom entry).

source.description:
`known` (the bundled list; an `agents.toml` entry of the same name supplies its content), `service` (the same, an
API key service) or `custom`.

Action.description: What the window and the CLI ask of plugins (owner and window only).

oneOf.description: Turns a plugin on or off; on runs nothing until it is approved.
Sets one setting; a value of the wrong type is refused.
Runs one command now for the project of `session` (none = no project).

poll.description: Asks for the result of the run started before (the answer to the first ask said `running`).

oneOf.description: Moves the folder to `plugins/.removed/`, so a removal can be undone by moving it back.
The catalogue's plugins (`plugins_online.rs`); the network, so off every lock.
Installs or updates a plugin from the catalogue: off and not approved until the owner reviews it.

Action2.description: What the owner and the CLI ask of triggers.

oneOf.description: The owner's alone. A webhook trigger needs a `secret` of at least 16 characters.
The owner, or a token of the `trigger` scope. `data` is the payload, shown to the session as quoted data.

Advance.description: Ticket 1081: the core's auto-advance record of a task. Kept so a restart repeats no nudge and no card.

done.description: What was done once, as `nudge:<session>:<n>` and `card:<session>:<n>` (`n`: the stall's start), newest last.

review.description: Part B: `waits` (its Reviewer waits for a free seat) or `started` (the core started it), for the task's row.

round.description: Part B: the review rounds whose findings the core forwarded to the Builder.

stalled.description: The seats seen stalled and not moved since.

AgentUpdatePhase.description: A finished update that worked or was cancelled has no run: the row is back on its version.

oneOf.description: The command exited 0 but the version did not change.

AgentUpdateRow.description: What the window shows for one tool found on the PATH.

command.description: Display text for 명령 복사, only when `can_update`. The runner never reads it; `start` takes the tool alone.

installer.description: Tools naming the same installer must not update at once (`start` refuses the second); `None`: the tool updates itself.

text.description: The last line the updater printed, sampled; installers report no percent.

AgentView.description: What the agent approval sheet shows: the exact command it would run.

refused.description: Why this entry can never launch as it is (a Claude entry without an API key or cloud credential set).

Alias.description: Ticket 1068: an alias with the `HostName` and `User` its config Host block names (first value wins, as in ssh).

oneOf.description: V2-8e: deny, with a one-line instruction for the agent (`deny_note`); empty text is a plain deny.
V2-8e: the agent's own session-only "don't ask again" option (`Decision::allow_always`); never one that persists.

Home look S2-7 (11-17): a question's free-text choice (Claude's "Type something.", `Choice::takes_text`) with the
words to type there, one line (`deny_note`'s rules).

ApprovalLevel.description:
What a user may grant. Never (answer decisions, change settings, touch agent config) has no API,
so it is not a level; `Act` implies `Read`.

oneOf.description: Approved once, but a file changed since.

act_refused.description: v1b-34: why act cannot be granted for this content (a web widget naming a script CDN host).

added.description: A plugin's access beyond what was approved (`plugins::access` lines): why it asks again.

extras.description: A plugin's shortcuts and status items, as its access lines (the sheet lists them under its parts).

hash.description: The hash a grant must quote, so the user approves exactly what the sheet showed.

parts.description: A plugin's panels and commands with what each runs (the sheet lists them; `manifest.command` is empty).

read_home_wide.description: v1b-33: a `read` entry covers the user's whole home (`home_wide` against the core's HOME); the sheet warns.

updated.description: A plugin approved for its access whose files changed since, asking for nothing new: it stays approved.

Approved.description: An approval, only ever the user's own (no session sets one): who and when.

asking.description:
Look 1117 v12 B N11-S2-3: the turn works, but it blocks in `agent ask --wait` on its open ask
(`Sessions::asks_waiting`). Set per snapshot, never stored; left out while false.

input_blocked.description:
v19-Q9-cx: the agent does not read its terminal: the last write was refused (`Pty::input_blocked`). Set per
snapshot, never stored; left out while false.

working_since.description:
Q7 item 12: when the current turn began (ms); the tree row shows how long it has been working. Left out while 0,
so a session that never worked keeps the legacy wire byte for byte (tests/board_transport.rs).

AuthMethod.description:
One sign-in method as the agent reported it, bounded. `kind` is `agent` or `terminal` only: a browser and a device code
are both `agent` (ACP cannot tell them apart), and `env_var` is left out, since Nunchiro stores no key.

Background.description: The lead's own text: what came before, what is decided, what must not change.

oneOf.description: The sha512 equals the hash cdnjs published for this library, version and file.
Pinned at first fetch, not checked against a published hash.

Base.description:
What the session's folder was when it started. A session record without one (started before
v1b-11) has no base: Diff says "start commit unknown" and never falls back to today's HEAD.

oneOf.description: A repository with no commit yet: everything is compared with the empty tree.

Blocker.description: A task this one waits for, as a reader gets it.

dropped.description: It closed without landing (dropped, or its worktree removed): the waiting task asks instead of waiting.

stage.description: `plan`, `build`, `review`, `gate` (`stage`), or how it closed when that was not a landing (`dropped`).

project.description: An integration card's own `project`, or a manual card's linked session's project.

agent.description: "claude", "codex", or an ACP agent as `acp:<its name in agents.toml>` (`agent_key`).

id.description: The teammate id, unchanged by the move.

BotsSeat.description: One Chief for the office (Home), one Lead per project; a bot with no seat works for whoever opens it.

Branch.description: Whether the Branch scope can compare in this folder.

oneOf.description: `default` is origin's default branch as a remote branch name, such as `origin/main`.
HEAD is on the default branch itself: there is no other branch to compare.

BranchPr.description: Ticket 373: the PR of a worktree's own branch, whoever opened it (an agent, or the person on GitHub).

state.description: In the order tier 1 reads a PR (`pr_live::parse`).

Breakdown.description: Ticket 1059: Claude's /context "Estimated usage by category" table, as its transcript record wrote it.

at.description: When Claude wrote the record, epoch ms.

rows.description: Empty: the record was there but its table could not be read.

Brief.description:
The instruction text a seat received with its first prompt from `task staff` (the lead's words, or the core's
review prompt), kept as sent. The package block and the notes head in front of it are not repeated here.

BrowserStatus.description: Settings > Browser access: what the window shows and changes (window only, `BrowserFrame`).

oneOf.description: Written by the core itself (an ask's timeout), not on behalf of a seat. No guard counts it as an agent message.

adds.description: How many of each kind it adds (`panel`, `command`, `setting`, `check`).

commit.description: The commit its files are read at (40 hex).

dir.description: Its folder in the repository at that commit.

network.description: The hosts its parts may reach.

additions.description: Line counts; null for a binary file or an untracked file not counted.

old_path.description: The path at the start commit, for a rename or copy.

stamp.description:
Q9 pop-J25-1: the working file's stat as a number; null when it is gone. A second edit with the same counts
changes it, so Diff re-reads that patch.

Channel.description: What V2-12m-b's Machines page reads: the connection state and since when, and the remote's protocol.

error.description: Why the channel is not up; while it is up, what the owner must do on that machine (`ssh_login_note`).

latency_ms.description: Milliseconds from starting ssh to the relay hello: the one-shot status time of the last connection.

banner.description: Pinned version event; also appears at its normal history cursor. Consumers deduplicate it.

before.description: Exclusive cursor for the next older page; absent at the beginning.

end.description: Latest cursor, including when the page is empty.

no_transcript.description:
Ticket 212 (A5): why no transcript could be read for this session, in words. Absent while one is read, so
the wire of such a page stays byte-identical; the window shows it for a session that works without one.

acp_v1_ms.description: Milliseconds from the start of the handshake to a v1 `initialize` result.

auth_methods.description: Ticket 358: the sign-in methods the agent reports and this client can offer (`auth_methods`).

capabilities.description: What the agent says it can do (`agentCapabilities` entries that are true).

env_set.description: Per env name: whether the core has a value to pass. Never the value.

sign_in.description: The sign-in running for this agent, so a reloaded window finds it (filled in by `acp::setup`).

signed_in.description: True when `session/new` gave a session, false when it answered `auth_required`, none when it did not get there.

detail.description: `Other` only: git's last error line, credentials removed.

parent.description: A refusal that is about the parent folder, not the URL.

path.description: The target folder (also for `Exists`, which says which folder it did not touch).

removed.description: The folder this job claimed is gone again.

stage.description: git's progress label and its percent; the window translates the labels it knows.

how.description:
`done` (the lead or the user said so), `merged` (its last worktree went with nothing left outside the project),
`removed` (an unnamed task's worktree went with its branch kept), `dropped`.

CodexResetEntry.description: One line of the use log.

rule.description:
The policy rule that decided it (`off`, `conditions`, `expiring`, `weekly_not_used_up`, `week_max`,
`keep_last`, `none_left`, `ask`, `account_gone`, `codex_error`).

why.description: The agent's reason, cleaned and capped.

command.description: argv, run from the plugin folder; never a shell string.

hash.description: Only when the check passed: the hash the grant must quote.

CommandView.description: What the row shows. `state` is `None` when there is no override: new sessions run the agent found on PATH.

env_set.description: Per saved env name: whether the core has a value. Never the value.

pending.description: Passed the check and waits for the owner; new sessions do not use it.

display.description:
Ticket 358: the name the window shows instead of `name`. Only a label: outside the approval hash, so changing it
asks for no new approval.

Context.description: `context.json`: project display names and the session list with states; no paths, ids, transcripts or tokens.

Counts.description: The counts a brief and the digest give; no agent writes one.

active_days.description: Local days in the range with any tokens.

first_day.description: The local day (days since 1970-01-01 in local time) of `daily[0]`; `daily` runs 42 days to today.

hours.description: Tokens by local weekday and hour, Monday 00:00 first (7 x 24), over the range.

DiffScope.description:
Ticket 374: what a diff request compares with. `Branch` is where HEAD left origin's default branch, from the
last fetched origin (no network); behaviour from t3code apps/web/src/components/DiffPanel.tsx:678-700 (MIT).

DigestRow.description:
Home view change 1 (11-17): one registered project as the Home view's Projects part shows it. Every number is the
core's, from the ledger, the decision queue and the sessions; no agent writes one.

at.description: The newest change: when (ms) and one line (a task's title or a session's name).

lead.description: The project's lead (a teammate id); none: the row is never counted for that.

lead_state.description:
Look 11-17 v5 item 4: "failed" when the lead's seat session failed and none of its sessions runs; look 11-17 v9
(Home S2-3): "missing" when the project's folder is gone; absent else. Either needs the user.

merged.description: Since the window was last there (`since`, ms): tasks merged and decisions that came.

needs.description: Pending decisions only: its sessions' asks and the owner cards about it, as Decisions and the tree count them.

oldest.description: The oldest of those, which "Answer" opens.

Draft.description: What the Create PR form starts with (`pr_draft`). All text is git's or the repository's: the window draws it as text.

bases.description: The default branch first, then the remote's other branches.

commits.description: Commits the PR holds (against the default branch).

gh_why.description: Why gh cannot create it now (not installed, not signed in); the form still opens.

push.description: Where the push goes first; `ahead` 0 when nothing needs pushing.

template.description: The body is the repository's PR template.

id.description: Increasing within a core; a later core starts above the earlier one (`Log::new`).

type.description:
`session_started`, `state`, `session_ended`, `worktree_created`, `worktree_removed`, `room_message`,
`room_pins` (ticket 593: the room's pin list after a change, `data` {log, pins}), `schedules_changed` (the
schedule list changed: no project, session or data; a reader reads the list again).

ExtensionsFileEntry.description: One file of an item, `path` relative to the item and `/` separated.

Failed.description:
Ticket 373: one failing check, outside text: the window shows it as text and a link, and the fix prompt wraps it as
untrusted data.

FailedRun.description:
Ticket 993 rule 6: a schedule whose last run failed, for the digest: which schedule (its id, and `line`, the
sentence its card would say) and why. It stays until the schedule runs again, is edited or is removed.

session.description: The session it started, when it got that far.

FastCooldown.description:
Ticket 1010: `text` is Claude's notice before its "· resets in 5m" ("Fast limit reached, fast mode paused"), `until`
the epoch second that "in 5m" pointed at when the notice came. Both absent: the faint ↯ alone was read.

data.description: Raw bytes of an image up to 2 MB.

hash.description: Ticket 820: SHA-256 (hex) of the bytes read, with `text`; `file_write` takes it back to refuse a changed file.

mtime_ms.description:
v1b-09: modification time at read, ms since the Unix epoch (0 if the platform has none), so the window
can tell a same-size edit of a file over 2 MB.

text.description: Text, Markdown, SVG and HTML up to 2 MB.

git.description:
One git status letter (`M`, `A`, `D`, `R`, `?`, ...); a folder shows `?` when untracked and `M`
when something beneath it changed. Null outside a git repository and for clean entries.

Fill.description: What a `task package` verb carries besides its text (`Request::Task.package`).

First.description: A bot's first chat, as the window draws it.

seat.description: The seat its template asks for: the chat asks the owner where it sits.

wrote.description: The bot wrote its SOUL file: the chat shows it on a card, with Undo.

path.description: The binary on the core's PATH (Settings > Accounts shows it).

sessions.description: Transcripts the agent's own folder lists.

version.description: `--version` output of the binary found; `None` when missing or when the probe failed.

Fix.description: A fix the window asks for on an ended session. Owner and window only.

Folder.description:
Ticket 1123: one folder an agent worked in, for onboarding's Folder row. No title field: the type cannot carry the
words of a conversation (a first message can hold a secret).

agent.description: The agent of the newest conversation there.

gone.description: Not a folder on this Mac now (moved or deleted).

FolderState.description: Ticket 1040: what Settings > Projects says about a project's folder.

oneOf.description: Not there, and its disk is.
On an external disk that is not mounted: nothing to locate, the disk comes back.
EPERM or EACCES: the folder may be there, the app may not read it.

Gate.description:
A check run before an action: it answers `{"allow": true}`, `{"allow": false, "reason": "..."}` or, before a
message, `{"allow": true, "text": "..."}` to replace it. It can do nothing else.

command.description: argv, run from the plugin folder; 5 seconds at most.

on_error.description: What no answer, a crash or bad JSON means.

oneOf.description: A new agent session is about to start (not a plain terminal, not a resumed conversation).
A message an agent, a schedule or a token sends is about to be delivered; never what the owner types.

GitFacts.description:
Ticket 373: what the Diff header's one git button reads (web/src/diff/gitAction.ts, after T3 Code's
`resolveQuickAction`). Read only, like the rest of this module: the button only asks the session's agent.

ahead_of_default.description: Commits on HEAD that origin's default branch lacks; null when that branch is unknown.

branch.description: The checked-out branch; null when HEAD is detached.

gh.description: `gh` is on the core's PATH (the PATH the PR poller uses); whether it is logged in is not known here.

head.description: The commit HEAD names; null before the first commit. The Push strip shows it and sends it back.

is_default.description: The checked-out branch is the default branch: one press must never push there.

push_to.description: Where the app's Push sends the branch (git_write.rs `target`); null with `push_why` saying why there is none.

upstream.description: The branch has an upstream; `ahead` and `behind` count against it (0 without one).

upstream_unknown.description:
Ticket 393: the branch has an upstream set that cannot be read as an exact `refs/heads/` ref (or the read
failed): where a push lands is unknown, so the button offers no push or PR; a commit still is.

Github.description: What a GitHub trigger watches: one repository and one kind of event.

any_author.description:
Pull requests of anyone, not only the owner's own (`--author @me`): on a public repository a stranger's pull
request could then start a run on code the stranger wrote.

label.description: The label a `labeled` trigger waits for.

oneOf.description: An open pull request's checks failed (once per head commit).
A review asked for changes on an open pull request (once per head commit).
An open issue or pull request has the label.

Group.description: One row of a tab: an agent, a model, a folder or an agent session.

account.description: The account id ("own" or a registry id) a session ran on.

parts.description: New input, output, cache write, cache read.

sessions.description: Distinct agent sessions in the row.

unpriced.description: Tokens of models `PRICES` does not list (in `tokens`, not in `cost_micro`).

n.description: Its place among the session's matching events, in chat order: the event id `sessions_hit` resolves.

text.description: The matching text around the first match, on one line.

oneOf.description: The holder is older than this core: "Needs restart after update" (Restart session).
The holder is newer than this core: not attached, "Update Nunchiro".

HookLine.description: One hook command: on `event`, for tools matching `matcher` (empty: every one), runs `command`.

oneOf.description: The owner's own click (window or owner socket).
The owner allowed an agent's ask in the Decisions widget.
Used for an agent under "allow ahead" without asking.
An agent's ask, waiting in the Decisions widget.

ImportItem.description: One conversation as the window shows it. `id` is `<agent>:<file stem>`.

ran.description: Ticket 1073: a conversation a Nunchiro session ran (`ran.json`), so History never calls it started in a terminal.

queued.description:
V2.5-21 (WP3): when the agent sent it (microseconds since the Unix epoch). The app drops a job sent before the owner's
last Hand back of the space, so a verb queued before or during his takeover never runs on the page he changed.

id.description: The launch call's id: one launch, one child, however many records replay it.

started_at.description:
The launch record's own `timestamp` as epoch seconds: the one time the transcript states. Absent when the record
carries none (a kind or version that dates nothing), which is why it is not a `Working` fact by itself.

oneOf.description: The agent said it is working: an ACP `subagent_update` running or requires_action.

Launched, but the evidence never said how it ended. One with a `started_at` is read as running by the tree;
one without stays unknown and is shown as nothing.

KidsSource.description: Where an opened sub-agent's rows come from.

oneOf.description: The child's own transcript file.
No child file (ACP, older agent, not written yet): the parent's chat, at the launch call.

reason.description: One line on why it failed.

result.description: Absent: the session still works on it.

session.description: The session the run started or sent its task to; absent when it could not start.

LedgerSeat.description: One session of a role on this task. Never reused: a second builder after the first ended is a second seat.

briefed.description: Slice h: its first prompt from the lead carried the notes it reads.

writes.description: Whether this seat changes files. One live writer per worktree.

LedgerView.description: A task as a reader gets it: the record, and what the core worked out now.

accounts.description: Ticket 1120: each seat's account label (session id to label); a seat on its lead's own default is not listed.

advance.description: Ticket 1081: what the core's auto-advance (advance.rs) did for its seats; empty until it first acts.

after.description:
The tasks of the same place it waits for, at most `AFTER_MAX`. Whether it still waits is worked out at each read
(`blockers`): one closed as merged or done holds it no more. A build without the field reads the file and drops
it on its next write.

asking.description:
The seats (session ids) with an open ask: they wait for the answer, also while their turn runs the wait. The
window reads the state from the seats again with it (look 1117 v11 B N11-S2-3).

asks.description: Open room asks of its seats, as "from → to: words".

auto.description: Made by the core for a lead's worktree that named no task: its title is the worktree's name.

blockers.description: The tasks of `after` that have not landed (`blockers`).

early.description: A seat that writes sat on it before it waited: `started before "<title>" landed`.

floor.description:
Ticket 1055 rule 2: a seat that does not write runs its role's own model, so the floor of its Builder's level
could not apply. One plain line.

lead.description: The lead (team.rs teammate id) it was made for; a teammate id, so the task outlives the lead's session.

learned.description:
Slice h: lessons its seats proposed, at most `LEARNED_KEPT`. They are no notes: the user's yes on the merge
card copies one to `notes.json`; a dropped task's lessons go with it.

live.description: The seats whose session runs now.

merge.description: Slice h: the user's yes to the merge, for the files at this revision only.

ordered.description: Who last changed `after`, so a lead's handover reads who ordered it.

package.description: Ticket 1095: the task's work package, read for `show` and the package verbs only (its own file).

place.description: The project root, or the Home folder.

released.description: The tasks of `after` whose landing or drop its lead was told (advance.rs `release`), so a restart tells it once.

seen.description: Ticket 1081: each seat's last activity (ms), for "N min ago".

stale.description: A review exists and the worktrees are no longer at its revision.

stall.description: Ticket 1004: what its seats' check-ins found; absent until the first one.

state.description:
`needs` (a seat waits for the user), `working`, `review` (a reviewer runs, or the files changed after the
review), `changes` (the review asked for changes), `approved` (the review passed and nothing changed since),
`merge` (approved, and the user said yes to merging these files), `asked` (no seat works and one of its room asks
is open), `idle`, or how it closed.

stuck.description: A task it waits for was dropped: what the user is asked (the state is then `needs`).

waiters.description: How many open tasks wait for this one.

waits.description:
Ticket 1081: what waits on the lead: `review` (a done report newer than the last review, no seat at work) or
`merge` (approved).

name.description: Who proposed it, as the card shows it ("Reviewer · review-tax").

role.description: The proposer's role, the default when the user keeps it as a role note.

first_requester.description: The session (or widget) whose page first asked.

path.description: The canonical path rebuilt from the tuple, with its leading `/`.

orchestration_override.description: The folder whose files replace the built-in orchestration skill's.

Limit.description: V2.5-10: an agent's own record of a usage limit, still ahead (Codex rollouts carry it; Claude's transcripts do not).

LinkStatus.description: Why a link in the user's own default folder was or was not read.

oneOf.description: Followed, but the linked scan's own file or byte cap ran out: the numbers are a lower bound.
The target is outside the user's home and every volume the owner named.
The target is not a folder, cannot be read, or is writable by others.

unavailable.description: "script widgets unavailable: <reason>" when the sandbox is missing or failed its self-check.

web_enabled.description: v1b-22: the `web_widgets` setting (`enabled` and `unavailable` are about script widgets only).

Listed.description: One row of the Plugins page.

blocked.description: Why the catalogue it came from blocks it (its kill list): it is off and cannot be turned on.

needs.description: The setting that is off and stops this plugin's parts (`script_widgets` or `web_widgets`).

skipped.description: Its checks that got no time in an action's budget since the core started (the action went by `on_error`).

state.description: Absent when the folder or its manifest cannot be read (`error` says why).

updated.description: Changed since its approval but asking for nothing new (`approval::View::updated`): still approved.

values.description: The current value of each setting (stored, else the default).

Live.description: What the window gets for one PR.

LogProblem.description: What is wrong with the log, for the Usage page.

set_aside_at.description:
When a log that could not be read was moved aside within the last 7 days (Unix seconds): agents' automatic
uses are refused until 7 days after, as their weekly count went with it.

unreadable.description: The log file cannot be read now (the next log write moves it aside).

oneOf.description: The user owes it to `who`.
The user waits for it from `who`.

asked.description: Its overdue card was raised once: a card the user dismissed does not come back.

due.description: `YYYY-MM-DD` in the user's local time: the row is overdue from the day after.

id.description: "L3"; empty until the row is stored.

source.description: Where it came from: an Outbox card, a mail id or the user's words.

Manifest.description: What the sheet shows, from the parsed manifest and never from text the author wrote about it.

command.description: The exact argv; empty for a web widget.

V2.5-20: one `nunchiro browser` verb, run in the calling session's own space (session callers only).
V2.5-20: the app takes the next browser job (owner only; waits up to `browser::POLL`).
V2.5-20: the app's answer to job `id` (owner only).
V2.5-15 (ticket 154): the wizard's folder, a new Git repository; owner and window only.

parent.description: Ticket 370: `~/` or absolute, no `..`; `~/Projects` when absent.

oneOf.description: Ticket 370: `git clone` of a typed URL into `parent`; answers at once. Owner and window only.

V2.5-15: opens a known project, or a file inside one, in the user's editor (`open -t`, or `open -a` the app in
`editor-app`); a path outside every known project is refused. Owner and window only. Ticket 375: also a
session's folder or a managed worktree; the app chosen in Settings (`editor.app`) wins over `editor-app`; `line`
jumps there in an editor with a URL handler (VS Code, Cursor, Zed), else the file opens at its top.
Ticket 375: which known editor apps are in /Applications or ~/Applications (Settings' editor row). Owner only.
V2.5-15: a chosen image (PNG, JPEG or SVG, at most 256 KiB, base64) as a known project's icon.
Ticket 1040: the folder state of every known project (Settings > Projects). Owner only.

Ticket 1040 (Locate): the project at `from`, whose folder moved, is the folder `to` from now on; everything the
core stores under `from` moves with it, all or nothing (`sessions::locate`). Owner only.
V2.5-11 (needs 136): scheduled runs, owner only (`schedule`).

at.description: Local `HH:MM`, or `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM` for a once-schedule with a date.

days.description: Ticket 993: the days of the week a daily entry runs on (0 Sunday to 6 Saturday, sorted); empty: every day.

replace.description:
Ticket 991 C3: the schedule this one replaces (Edit), in the same write; `None` adds a new one. Ticket 993:
the edited entry keeps the replaced one's switch (`paused`), and its last run unless that failed.

oneOf.description: Ticket 993: the entry runs once now, also when it is switched off; its next time does not move. Owner only.
Ticket 993: switches an entry off (`paused`) or on again. Owner only.

Ticket 993: the lead of a place proposes a schedule for a teammate of its place, by name
(`nunchiro schedule propose`). `when` is `daily HH:MM`, `weekdays HH:MM`, `weekly <day> HH:MM` or
`once YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM`. Nothing is stored: the user gets a card (`queue::OwnerAsk::Schedule`) and only its
yes adds the entry. Refused to every other caller and to a session that does a scheduled run.

A bot's seat offers the user a new bot for work it saw come back (`nunchiro bot offer`): `why` is what it
counted. Nothing is made: the user gets a card (`queue::OwnerAsk::Bot`) and only its yes makes the bot, in the
offering bot's place. Refused to every caller that is no bot's seat.

A bot's seat reads or changes its own memory (`nunchiro memory`): `operation` is `add` (`text` one fact;
`topic` a topic file; `user` the shared USER.md; `from_user` the user said it), `forget` (`text`: words of the
line) or `read` (`topic`, or the index). Nunchiro adds the date and the source; once the seat read outside
content (mail, web, another MCP server) an add waits as a proposal. Refused to every caller that is no bot's
seat. Reply: `Text`.
Ticket 993: a lead asks to `pause`, `resume` or `remove` (`change`) a schedule it may read; a card, as above.

Ticket 1002 lane 2: the Home lead stages one outward tool call as the user's Outbox card (`nunchiro outbox
stage`): `tool` the exact tool name it will call (a Gmail `send_message`, `reply`, `forward`; a calendar
`create_event`), `args` the exact arguments, each one shown on the card (any other is refused). Nothing is sent.
Refused to every other caller; a scheduled run of the Home lead may stage. Reply: `Text` (the card in words).

Ticket 1002 lane 2: the Home lead's seat (its hook, before the tool runs) asks to make the outward call `tool`
whose `approval::outward_call_hash` is `args_hash`. `Text { text: <card id> }` once, when an approved, unspent
card has exactly that call (it is spent then); otherwise an error, and the call must not run.

V2.5-30: `agent list`, the sessions a `session list` shows; `mine` keeps the calling session's direct children
(the caller is the token's or the peer-checked session, never an argument; refused outside every session).

Ticket 372: arm (`on`) or cancel one resume of session `id` at the reset its limit line shows; owner and window
only. The core then sends the fixed continue text once, at that reset.

The owner is typing for session `id` (the window's composer or terminal); carries no text. Another sender's
queued message waits `TYPING_QUIET` after the last one. Owner and window only.

The owner's choice on another sender's queued message `send` of session `id` (the knock): send it now (no wait
for his typing), later (after his next prompt's turn), attached to his next prompt, or detached again (later).
Owner and window only.
The window's composer took the words `draft_home` gave it; their side file goes. Owner and window only.

at.description: The hand-over taken (`draft_home.at`): an answer to an older one leaves newer words alone.

oneOf.description: ⌘Z on words that came home: they go back into the agent's empty box, with no Enter. Owner and window only.

⌘Z on another sender's message in the agent's box: its Enter is canceled, the box cleared, and the row waits as
Later. A message the agent already took is not undone. Owner and window only.

Type in terminal (`on`) for session `id`: the owner types in the agent's own box; another sender's message waits
(`direct`). It ends by itself 60 s after the last key in that terminal or the last renewal. Owner and window only.

Ticket 990: a lead opens the seat of a teammate of its place, by name (`nunchiro team open <name>`). Only the
place's lead seat may; the seat starts as its worker, with the teammate's own brief as its first prompt.

level.description: Ticket 992: the level the lead asks for this task (`--level`); absent asks none.

oneOf.description:
Ticket 990 slice g: the job ledger (`ledger.rs`). `operation`: `new` (`text` is the outcome, `accept` its
conditions), `list`, `show`, `attach` (a worktree at `path` to task `id`), `assign` (`session` sits on a task
that uses no worktree), `pass` / `changes` (a review of what the worktrees hold now, `text` its note), `learn`
(a seat's lesson, `text`, for the merge card), `staff` (`text` is a role's name: what to
start for that seat), `way` / `grant` (the owner's choice for the place, `text`), `merge` (the lead asks the user to merge an approved task: a
card), `done`, `drop`, `package-<part>` and `brief` (ticket 1095). The owner and a place's lead make and close tasks; only a seat that does not write, or the owner,
reviews. `project` is read for the owner only; a session's place is its lead's.

account.description:
Ticket 1120, `staff`: the account label the seat starts on (`--account`); absent: the place's account,
else the caller's own.

after.description: `new` and `after`: the ids of the tasks of the same place it waits for; `after` with none clears them.

cites.description: `learn`: a repo-relative file the lesson is about.

effort.description:
Ticket 1054, `staff`: the effort the seat opens at (`--effort`), one of its agent's efforts; absent keeps
the level's.

level.description: Ticket 993 rule 9, `staff`: the level the seat opens at (`--level`); absent asks none, which is standard.

package.description:
Ticket 1095, `package-<part>` (`nunchiro task package`): what the verb carries besides `text`: who said a
quote and when, its images, a link's kind and whether a mockup is approved. `brief` (`seat_up`) needs none.

who.description:
Ticket 1003, `promise` and `waiting` (an open loop, `loops.rs`): who it is owed to or awaited from, and its
due date as `YYYY-MM-DD`. `text` is what; `loop-close` names the loop with `id` and says why in `text`.

why.description: Ticket 1099 panel 4, `ask-cap`: the lead's reason for the live-seat change it asks the user for.

oneOf.description:
Ticket 990 slice i: the user's roles (`roles.rs`). `list`: anyone. `save` (`role`) and `remove` (`name`): the
owner's only. `propose` (`role`, `why`): a place's lead asks the user on a card.

Ticket 990 slice h: accepted notes (`notes.rs`). `list`: the owner reads every note (flagged when its cited file
is gone); a session reads the ones for its place and role. The owner's only: `keep` (lesson `lesson` of task
`task` becomes a note in `scope`, or `text` with no task is the user's own note), `edit` (`id`, `text` and/or
`scope`), `remove` (`id`).

Ticket 571: the project's message room. The sender is the calling session (the person outside every session),
stamped by the core; no field names it. `project` is read for the person only; a session's room is its own.

Ticket 571c: the window's room panel reads the newest `ROOM_READ_MAX` messages of a project's room, read or not,
with no cursor moved. The owner's only: an agent reads its own inbox and threads, never the whole room.
`since` and `log` (the last message number and the log id a reply gave) ask only for what came after; a log that is
no longer that log, or a gap past the read cap, gets the newest messages again with `reset` set.
Ticket 593: the person pins (`pinned`) or unpins one message of a project's room; the owner's only, as `RoomRead`.
The reply to the caller's own ask, if any; `give_up` with none logs the ask's timeout event.

Resolved.description: One answer of [`Libs::resolve`], in the order asked.

oneOf.description: Serve `/lib/<sha384>`: the entry exists and its stored file hashes to the pin.

Not pinned (or its stored file is missing or changed): the card. `listed`: the manifest has this library,
version and file ("cdnjs lists this version"); `auto`: an auto-allowed fetch was started, the card shows
until the pin exists; `other_versions`: pinned versions of the same host, library and file ("Open with").

revision.description: What was reviewed: `revision` of every worktree of the task at that moment, in the task's order.

state.description: `requested`, or the review state (APPROVED, CHANGES_REQUESTED, COMMENTED, ...).

job.description: What a seat of this role does, in a few lines: it opens the seat's first prompt.

writes.description: Whether its seats change files. One live writer per worktree.

oneOf.description: An ask whose `--wait` ran out; `reply_to` is the ask.
The round cap stopped a thread; addressed to the person.

A seat ended (exited or failed) while an ask with it was open; `reply_to` is the ask. Sent by the ended seat to the
ask's other party: no answer will come, and none is needed.

Ticket 990: what one seat typed into another's terminal (a lead's prompt to its worker, a worker's line to its
lead when it finished). It was delivered there, so it is no unread message for its seat; the room keeps it so
the person reads the whole talk in one place.

Ticket 990: something happened to a lead's team (`Message::team` says what): a worktree made, removed, handed
over or taken back, or the user spoke to a sub-bot directly. Written by the core.

Saved.description: What settings.json holds for the alias, without what `ssh -G` adds: the Edit form starts from these.

at.description:
Local `HH:MM`, or `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM` for a once-schedule made with a date (ticket 333). Entries from before
dates have the bare time and keep working.

daily.description:
Fires every day at `at`; false: once. A once entry that fired stays listed, switched off (`paused`), with its
last run, until the user removes it or edits it (look 11-17 v8 Home S2-C: it vanished the moment it fired,
and nothing said that it ran). Entries from before load unchanged.

days.description:
Ticket 993: the days of the week a repeating entry runs on, sorted (0 Sunday to 6 Saturday, as JavaScript's
`getDay`). Empty, as in every entry from before: every day. Not written when empty, so an old entry keeps
its bytes and its MAC.

earlier.description:
Ticket 1002: the runs before `last`, newest first, at most `EARLIER_MAX` (outside the MAC). Not written when
empty, so an entry from before keeps its bytes.

last.description: Ticket 993: the last run, the core's own note (outside the MAC).

mac.description: Hex HMAC-SHA256 of `id`, `run`, `at` and `daily` (and `days`, when it has any) under `schedule.key`.

next_ms.description: Unix ms of the next fire (the core moves it, so it is outside the MAC).

paused.description:
Ticket 993: the user switched it off: it stays listed and does not run. `next_ms` means nothing while paused;
a resume sets it again. Like `next_ms`, outside the MAC.

ScheduleRun.description: What a schedule starts: the owner's closed choice, never a raw `StartSession`.

level.description:
Ticket 992: the level the teammate's seat opens at for this task (team.rs `open_seat`). Absent asks none and
is not written, so an entry from before levels keeps its MAC. Never stored for a teammate that leads its place
(look 11-17 v8: its seat is not replaced for a scheduled run).

task.description: Ticket 981: what the session is told when it starts. `None`: the session only opens.

teammate.description:
Ticket 981: the teammate (team.rs id) that does the task. Its folder, agent, name and brief are read at each
fire; `kind`, `project` and `label` here are what they were when the schedule was made, for the list.

status.description: `ok` (hits), `missing` (no transcript), `untested` (agent version whose chat shows final text only), `error`.

See.description: One thing the owner will see when the work is done.

approved.description: The owner's yes to the line; absent: not approved yet.

remote.description:
Ticket 76: whether a non-user sender was forwarded from another machine when the send was queued; the flush
reads this, not the lasting `grants.remote` set. Absent for `user`; absent on an agent row fails closed.

replaced.description: A plugin's check replaced what the sender wrote: the plugin and the original, so the owner sees both.

settle.description:
v1a-15: one of `SETTLE_MARKS` when the Enter went at the settle deadline or was dropped; absent
otherwise, so every other row serializes as before.

auto_label.description:
Ticket 1017: `label` came from the first message (`auto_title`, `codex_title`), not from the user; the window
numbers two equal such names ("ASK 1", "ASK 2"). A hand-set label clears it. Omitted when false.

closed_at.description:
Ticket 621: when the row went Closed (epoch ms); only the newest closed rows are kept. Absent on rows closed
before ticket 621, which count as the oldest.

closed_by_command.description:
Ticket 1013 F6: closed by a command (the CLI, a script, the lead, any core caller but the window's own Close); the
window drops its tab at once. Absent: the window keeps the done tab with Continue and Restart, as before.

ended_at.description:
Lane w59 (History run length): when this run ended (epoch ms), stamped once by the core that saw it end: the
agent quit (its shell may stay), the process exited, or the core stopped it. Absent on a run still going, on
one a close ended (`closed_at` is its end) and on rows that ended before this field or while no core watched.

home_lock.description:
Ticket 1002 lane 1: this Claude session runs with the Home seat lock (`home_lock`): a Home seat, or a session one
started. A session it starts carries the lock too. Set by the core at spawn, never taken from a request.

home_mode.description: Ticket 1002 lane 1 (Fable review R5): the lock's mode this run started in (`home_lock::name`); absent when not locked.

level.description:
Ticket 992: the level a seat was started at (team.rs `open_seat`); absent on a seat with a custom model and on
every other session.

modes.description: W35 picker: a Claude session's fast mode and ultracode as far as Nunchiro knows them (`sessions/claude_modes.rs`).

owned_from.description:
Codex security MUST (w20-h): the runs whose started sessions this run may close and list as `--mine`
(`Sessions::started_by`). Only a resume the owner or the core made carries them; an agent's own
`session start --resume` keeps `resumed_from` (names only) and gets none.

ran_mode.description:
Look 11-17 N2: the last permission mode Claude's footer showed while the session ran (stored, unlike
`permission_mode`), so a resume starts in the mode the session ran with. Ticket 991 (B6 chip): for Codex, the
stored choice the owner's start applied (none when the arguments stated the permission, and on older rows).

resumed_from.description:
Look 1117 v10 N10-S2-3: the ids of the runs this resumed run continues, newest first (their rows are gone). A
room line names the seat by its old id; the window finds the seat's name through this.

schedule.description:
Ticket 993: the schedule (its id) whose run this session does unattended: set when a scheduled run starts the
session or sends its task to it, cleared when the user speaks to it. While set, the session may not propose
or change schedules. (A schedule's row names its last run's session itself: `Entry::last`.)

started_at.description:
Ticket 1025: when this run started (epoch ms), for History's start time and run length. Absent on rows
started before it.

starting.description:
Look 11-17 v3 P1: a new Claude session whose input box has not shown yet; a first message waits in the window
until it has (a startup question may still come, and text typed before the box is lost). Set per snapshot.

teammate.description:
Ticket 990: the teammate (team.rs id) whose seat this session is, stored when the core opens the seat and kept
by a resumed run. The lead of a place is found by it, so a lead outlives its session.

token_origin.description:
Ticket 573 round 6: the outside token (`token-<id>`) this session acts for, stored once at its start from the
caller, the run it continues or its side chat's main session, and copied into every continuation. Never
recomputed from live records and never cleared, so a closed or resumed parent changes nothing.

SessionLimit.description: Ticket 372: `resets` as the agent printed it, `until` its epoch second.

oneOf.description: `HH:MM`, 24-hour.

Settings.description:
`[settings]` in board.toml. `done_days` (1, 7 or 30, default 7, ticket 1066) is how long a finished card stays in
the Done column before it moves to the Archive. `stale_minutes` is the stale badge threshold (1 to 1440, default 10);
`turn_end_nudge` turns ticket 187's turn-end context line on or off (default true). One struct for both keys:
`deny_unknown_fields` refuses any other key.

Setup.description:
What the add steps show for a listed agent: how to install it, how it signs in, what it costs. From this bundled table
only; the window types the install command into a terminal tab and never runs it.

account.description: The service named in "With your {account} account".

checked.description: The day the cost line was read on the vendor's page (YYYY-MM-DD).

cost.description: free_plan, free_limited, free_models, own_model, paid_plan, paid_key or unknown.

install.description: The package-manager form, as an argv.

install_script.description: The vendor's one-line installer, when it is the only documented way.

sign_in.description: The agent's own sign-in command for the terminal fallback.

SetupView.description: What the setup approval sheet shows: the exact text that would run, and where.

path.description: The worktree the script was read from and would run in.

Show.description: Where a command's output goes: a note, a panel, or the focused agent's composer as a draft (never sent by itself).

SignIn.description: What the window polls for one `agent` sign-in; a terminal method is a tab, not an attempt.

link.description: Only ever a link `account_signin::allowed_acp` let through. Copied by the owner; the core does not open it.

SkipPermissions.description:
Bypass permissions (Claude `bypassPermissions`) for one session. `Unavailable`: Claude's Shift+Tab cycle has no such
mode (the session was not launched with the flags that list it); `Available`: pickable; `Disabled`: Claude's own
settings turn it off (`permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode`); `NeedsSetting`: not in this session's cycle and the
stored choice is Ask, so a new session would not have it either.

oneOf.description: `nunchiro trigger fire <name>`.

`POST http://127.0.0.1:<port>/hooks/<name>`, signed (GitHub `X-Hub-Signature-256`) or with
`X-Nunchiro-Secret`.
An event read from GitHub with the user's own `gh` (`github.rs`).

Stall.description:
Ticket 1004: a task's check-ins. A check-in is a seat's turn that ended and was told to its lead (sessions/wake.rs).
Progress is what the core records itself: the task's record (`updated`: a seat, a review, a worktree, the user's
words) and its worktrees' files (`revision`). Never what an agent wrote.

card.description: Its card was raised. One per stall: a card the user dismissed does not come back until the task moved.

error.description: The last check-in's error (a failed seat's cause; empty: none), and how many in a row said the same.

mark.description: `updated` and the revision at the last check-in; empty when the task has no worktree that could be read.

quiet.description: Check-ins in a row that found `mark` as the one before left it.

Stalled.description: One stalled seat: `why` is a plain line ("quiet for 20 min"), `at` the nudge's time, `n` the stall's start.

command.description: One of this plugin's commands, run when the item is pressed.

oneOf.description: A plugin folder, stored by its id; asked for and granted as the widget name `plugin:<id>` (`plugins.rs`).

Sum.description:
The v4 Usage page (usage.html v4, lane v25c-usage-split): sums over a rolling range for its tiles, token mix, busy
hours and tabs, and the 42 local days of its intensity grid. Read from the same local records as `rows`, in the
same budget; nothing is stored. Lifted from Orca (MIT License, Copyright (c) 2026 Lovecast Inc.; 1.4.214): the
cache share (cache read / (new input + cache read), `usage-overview-model.ts:72-73`) and the 42-day window
(`UsageOverviewPane.tsx:13`).

parts.description: New input, output, cache write, cache read.

unpriced.description: Tokens of models `PRICES` does not list (in `tokens`, not in `cost_micro`).

Summary.description: What a read shows: the available count and the earliest expiry (Unix seconds) among available credits.

Target.description:
Where a web widget's act goes: a running session labelled `session` in the placement's project, or a new
`start` agent there. Exactly one.

TeamLevel.description: Ticket 992: how much a task needs. Ordered, so Auto's upper limit is a `min`.

TeamNote.description: What happened to a lead's team. `worktree` is the worktree's folder; `seat` the sub-bot's session.

merged.description: On `removed`: nothing was left that the project does not have (no uncommitted file, no commit off its HEAD).

agent.description: Ticket 994: the ACP agent's name in `agents.toml` when `kind` is ACP; absent for Claude and Codex.

lead.description:
Ticket 990: this teammate leads its place (its project, or Home): at most one per place. The others of the
place are its team, and it may open them (`nunchiro team open`).

level.description:
Ticket 992: the level rule. Absent: Auto (the asked level, no level asked is standard); else pinned to this
level. A teammate with a `model` is "Custom model": no level applies to it.

level_max.description: Ticket 992: Auto's upper limit; an asked level above it opens at it. Ignored when pinned.

name.description: Also the session's label, so the room knows the seat by it.

next_level.description:
Ticket 992 rule 6: the level the user picked on the seat's row for this teammate's next task; the next open
that asks a level (or none) takes it and clears it.

source.description: The pinned raw URL it came from.

license.description: SPDX id as published, `unknown` or `nonfree` included.

hash.description: Lowercase hex SHA-256 of the secret. Never sent in a reply (`listed`).

project.description: Only sessions, worktrees and the room of this project (canonical); `None` is every project.

oneOf.description: List, get, read, wait, room check and thread read.
Read, plus start, prompt/send, room send/ask/reply, and stop of the sessions this token started.
What a session token may do, except answers, keys and settings (no scope has those); types only into its own.
Fires triggers (`nunchiro trigger fire`) and nothing else.

Told.description: What the user said to a seat directly, in the user's words (masked and cut by the caller).

TooLarge.description: An agent config past `MAX_AGENT_FILE`: its servers are not shown, and the page says why.

added.description: F15: projects added by picking their folder, shown with no session until removed (`Add` false).

folded.description:
Fold keys, two shapes: `group:<name>` is a folded group. `quiet:<name>` and `quiet:` (the ungrouped "Other
projects" line) are the quiet lines the owner has opened, because quiet lines start folded (needs 89).

names.description: 370: the names the owner chose, by project path; a project not listed reads as its folder name.

oneOf.description: A group is born with its first member: the project moves in from any other group.
Members become ungrouped.

`index` is the place among the target group's projects once the moved one has left it (so it is also the final
place); absent appends, past the end clamps. Added for the Undo of a move; an older client sends none.
F15: a picked folder is a project before any session starts in it; `added` false removes it again.
370: the name shown for a project; empty goes back to its folder name.
Restores a prior folding exactly.

fired.description: The starts of the last hour (unix ms), for `PER_HOUR`. Outside the MAC.

github.description: A GitHub trigger's repository and event.

last.description: The last fire: the session it started, or why not. Outside the MAC.

mac.description: HMAC of name, on, run, mode, secret and github under `schedule.key`.

name.description: a-z, 0-9, - and _; the webhook path and the CLI's name.

secret.description: A webhook's shared secret, kept only in this 0600 file the core writes; never in a reply.

started_cards.description:
The cards whose Start already ran (newest last, at most 20), so a card a quit left behind starts nothing twice.
Outside the MAC.

Turn.description: The three flags are the scorecard's words: a prompt sent, an answer read, the turn's end seen.

failure.description:
Why the try failed: `no_answer`, `not_signed_in`, `error` (the agent's own words in `error`), `empty`, `no_end`
(it stopped before the turn ended) or `other`; none when it answered.

ms.description: From the start of the run to the turn's end (or to the failure).

text.description: The answer's first `TEXT_MAX` characters, control characters removed.

version.description: The agent's `--version`, as the check reads it.

limit_resets.description: V2-2c limit mark: the reset time as the agent printed it on a session's screen ("11pm"), while it is ahead.

limits_at.description:
Ticket 1036: when Claude Code last handed this account's limits to its status line (Unix seconds); the
`session` and `weekly` of a Claude row come from that record.

link.description: Ticket 211: the user's own default folder is a link; where it points and whether it was read.

partial.description: The request's work cap ran out before this row was fully counted: the numbers are a lower bound.

session.description: The 5-hour style window's remaining share and reset, from the newest local record; none when no source has one.

unpriced_models.description: Models seen in the last 7 days that `PRICES` does not list: the page says "cost unknown for" them.

V1.description:
What today's team rules still read and a Bot has no word for yet, kept whole so a seat opens after the move
exactly as before it: the project of a bot with no seat, and ticket 992's level rule (`Teammate::level`,
`level_max`, `next_level`; `effort` is the one a follow-rule seat falls back to). Left out when empty.

Verb.description: The closed verb set (C4). No variant names a space, a session or a grant, and no variant carries script (Q1).

oneOf.description: A new tab in the caller's space, which becomes the current tab.
Indexed actionable elements plus visible text, viewport only; `tree` gives the role tree, `full` the whole page.
The agent needs the owner (a password, a captcha): the app tells the window; the agent stops.

act.description: The widget holds an `act` grant for this content.

hash.description: The approval hash of the folder the entry was read from (the app's frame id carries a prefix of it).

network.description: Approved manifest hosts that may appear in the frame's CSP (no IP literal, loopback or local name).

When.description: Ticket 993: when an entry runs. `at` and `daily` as on `Entry`; `days` only on a repeating one.

act.description: v1b-20: the `[act]` table while the widget holds a current act grant; rows are clickable only then.

state.description: Absent when the folder cannot be read or its manifest does not parse (`error` says why).

title.description: A plugin panel's title and its plugin's name (`plugin__<id>__<panel>` rows); absent for a widget folder.

project.description: Display name of the project the run saw; absent = no project.

running.description: Another caller's run of this widget is in progress; this is the last cached result.

Window.description: V2.5-10: what the last 24 h or 7 days (rolling, not local days) spent on one account.

cost_micro.description: List-price estimate in millionths of a US dollar, over the tokens of models `PRICES` knows.

unpriced.description: Tokens of a model `PRICES` does not know: in `tokens`, left out of `cost_micro`.

creator.description: v1a-16: session id of the token caller that created it; owner-created records have none.

facts.description: V2-8a: counted at list time for the reply only (never stored); absent for a missing folder.

root.description:
v25f: the worktree root the folder was made under (the setting may change since). A record from before has none
and is stamped with that time's root on the next run.

shared_failed.description:
Ticket 253: on the worktree a create just made, the shared paths (and the sparse preset) that failed, each as
`<path>: <reason>` (the window's create line). The reply only, never stored.

stale_base.description:
Ticket 374: on the worktree a create just made from origin's default branch when the fetch failed: that branch,
as last fetched, was used (the window's toast). The reply only, never stored.

team.description:
Ticket 990: the lead (team.rs teammate id) whose team this worktree is in: set when the lead's seat or one of
its workers creates it, or when the owner hands it over; absent for an independent worktree. A teammate id,
not a session id, so the team outlives the lead's session.

WorktreeCleaned.description: V2-8a: one auto-clean removal; the branch is kept, so `restore` with these fields is its Undo.

WorktreeFacts.description: V2-8a: a snapshot at list time. With no upstream, `unpushed` counts the commits not on the project's HEAD.

WorktreeLoss.description:
V2-8a: what a remove would lose: `git status --porcelain` lines and unpushed commits (`<sha> <subject>`), each
list cut at 200 with its full count; `kept_on` is the branch HEAD is on (`None`: detached, the commits go too).
`ignored`: git-ignored files a remove deletes too (`.env`, local config), less the build output `worktree_clean`
names (`target/`, `node_modules/`, ...), which can be rebuilt.

linked.description:
Ticket 253: the shared paths that are links to the project's own file (`worktree_shared`): listed, not lost, so
they count in no total.

too_large.description:
Coordinator 11-11 (v37-git-env R2): the status was past the read cap, so nothing is listed; `uncommitted_total`
is then the entries seen, a lower bound, and the confirm still removes (with `--force`).

WorktreeSetupAgent.description:
What the window's start-an-agent does after a create: `Wait` while the setup tab runs, `Start` when no setup ran or it
exited 0, `User` when it failed, was skipped or waits for approval (the start is left to the user).

WorktreeSetupStatus.description: The reply of `setup_status`: the repo script's sheet (absent with no repo script) and what start-an-agent does now.

description: Every line on the wire. A caller writes one envelope as a JSON line to $NUNCHIRO_HOME/core.sock and reads one response line back; `nunchiro events` prints event lines. A request variant's x-stability is stable (an outside token may call it; kept compatible) or window (the window's own; may change). See docs/api.md.
